links.outcome: Readability grade level of LLM consent answers
links.effect: Readability was appropriate (human: grade 7.5, 7.0-8.0; LLM: grade 6.4, 6.0-6.9).
links.quote: Readability was appropriate (human: grade 7.5, 7.0-8.0; LLM: grade 6.4, 6.0-6.9) and there was near identical semantic consistency (human: 0.91, 0.89-0.92; LLM: 0.91, 0.89-0.92).

links.outcome: Semantic consistency of consent LLM answers across repeated runs
links.quote: Readability was appropriate (human: grade 7.5, 7.0-8.0; LLM: grade 6.4, 6.0-6.9) and there was near identical semantic consistency (human: 0.91, 0.89-0.92; LLM: 0.91, 0.89-0.92).

links.outcome: Inter-rater reliability of accuracy ratings for human raters versus moderator LLM
links.effect: Human raters κ = 0.1 (0.0-0.2), indicating poor agreement; moderator LLM κ = 0.8 (0.8-0.8).
links.quote: Inter-rater reliability of accuracy ratings demonstrated significant differences between human assessors (κ = 0.1, 0.0-0.2) and the moderator LLM (κ = 0.8, 0.8-0.8).

unlisted_practices: Using a second moderator LLM to reproduce document-grounded accuracy assessments in place of human raters
Constraining an LLM to trial-specific documentation to answer informed consent questions

screen.reason: Evaluates the feasibility and accuracy of using an LLM constrained to trial documents to answer informed consent questions, as well as an LLM judge/moderator for evaluation, but does not test a specific comparative deployment safeguard/practice.
